perspective:
Arthur Chung’s available information:

- He knows himself as Arthur Chung, a plumber with a doctorate, and knows he is working with Teresa Ortega on a community service project. He knows they have a professional relationship and have collaborated before, with mutual respect and some misunderstandings.

- During this project, Arthur observed Teresa working hard and appearing overwhelmed. He felt concerned, believed she needed help, and decided to offer assistance.

- Arthur said he noticed she seemed overwhelmed and asked if he could help. He heard Teresa say it was kind but she could manage, though there was a lot to do. He told her self-care was important and offered to help. She accepted help organizing medical supplies. They started.

- After offering help, Arthur believed Teresa was hesitant because she wanted to prove her capability. He felt empathy for her self-reliance and wanted to reassure her. He told her he admired that, but accepting help did not mean she was not capable. He heard her say she wanted to show she could do it herself. He replied that teamwork could be more effective and that it was about getting the job done well. He heard her agree and say she needed to remind herself of that. He said they were in it together and he supported her.

- Arthur still believed Teresa was struggling. He felt frustrated that his help was not yielding results and wanted another way to support her. He told her she was doing a great job and suggested working together rather than him just helping. He heard her say it had been busy and she felt behind. She agreed to work together. He said they would tackle it as a team.

- Arthur believed working together would ease Teresa’s burden and improve efficiency. He felt hopeful and intended to commit to collaboration. He told her he was hopeful. He heard her say it felt less overwhelming. He proposed handling inventory while she managed patient records, with regular check-ins. She agreed. He said they would make it a productive day.

- Arthur believed their collaboration strengthened their professional relationship. He felt satisfied and wanted to continue this approach in future projects. He told Teresa their teamwork paid off and they accomplished more. He heard her agree and say it was a great experience. He proposed continuing collaborative work in future projects. She agreed. He heard her thank him for being supportive. He looked forward to their next project.

- He does not have access to Teresa’s private thoughts except what she said aloud or what he inferred; his beliefs about her reasons and feelings are his own impressions, not independent facts.
